9. Competitive Markets

Price is set where supply meets demand, and a tax wedged between them evaporates welfare exactly equal to the Harberger triangle.

  • Supply, Demand, and Equilibrium — The competitive equilibrium is where demand P=A−QP = A - QP=A−Q meets supply P=C+QP = C + QP=C+Q. Raise the per-unit tax ttt and a wedge opens between the buyer and seller prices, splitting consumer surplus, producer surplus, revenue, and deadweight loss in real time.
  • Tax vs Quota: Deadweight Loss — Taxes and quotas both shrink trade, but the lost welfare has the same shape. Switch instruments and watch the deadweight-loss triangle keep its area, while the transfer becomes tax revenue or quota rent.
